prompt:
I need the front end for Arrivals Commons Watch. The monitoring side of a university's private online community for admitted first-year students, used by the Office of New Student Programs and its student orientation leaders to follow activity and be alerted to the posts and patterns that need staff attention before move-in.

Who's using it: Renée Castellanos, assistant director of New Student Programs at a large public university, who oversees the admitted-student community with a team of 18 paid student orientation leaders acting as moderators. It is twelve days before move-in. She is trying to keep up with the busiest stretch of the year without reading every post.

What they're doing right now: Renée is back after a morning of orientation sessions and has three hours of activity to catch up on. A housing scam wave is likely: last August, fake sublet offers aimed at first-years showed up in exactly this week. She has to decide what needs her personally and what orientation leaders can handle: a reported post that may be a student in distress, a burst of near-identical 'cheap room near campus, Zelle deposit' messages from new accounts, and a roommate-matching thread where someone is posting other students' phone numbers. She also wants to change her alert rules so that routine questions about meal plans and parking stop interrupting her, while anything about safety, wellbeing or money reaches her right away, even when she is away from her desk at orientation.

What's in the system at this point: Community: Class of 2030, 4,212 admitted students joined of 5,040 confirmed, 61 groups (residence halls, majors, 'commuters', 'transfer-adjacent', 'first-gen', international by region), about 1,900 posts in the last 24 hours. Since 9:00: 7 student reports (1 wellbeing concern, posted 10:47 by an account in 'Hartwell Hall 2030'; 4 suspected scams; 2 personal-info exposures), 23 posts auto-held for links or payment terms, 14 questions unanswered for more than 6 hours, 9 accounts created today with no matching admissions record. Each orientation leader has an assigned set of groups and a status (on shift, in session, off). Current alert rules: notify on any report (too noisy), digest every 2 hours, quiet hours 23:00–7:00 except wellbeing. Escalation contacts: Counseling Center on-call line, Dean of Students office, University Police non-emergency, Housing fraud liaison D. Mbeki.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
